il_ez.label: Illinois Enterprise Zone
il_ez.desc: State-designated zones where businesses can get a sales-tax exemption on building materials, investment and jobs tax credits and local property-tax abatements (Illinois Enterprise Zone Act).

tif.label: Tax increment financing (TIF) district
tif.desc: Districts where the growth in property-tax revenue pays for redevelopment: public works, land and grants to projects, decided by the city, village or county that created the district. Texas calls them tax increment reinvestment zones, Georgia tax allocation districts, Florida community redevelopment areas; urban renewal and redevelopment areas in Oregon, Montana, Tennessee, Nevada and Iowa are financed the same way.

co_ez.label: Colorado Enterprise Zone
co_ez.desc: State-designated zones (Colorado Office of Economic Development) where businesses can claim state income-tax credits for investment, new jobs, job training and rehabilitating vacant buildings; the zones are large, often whole counties, and donors to approved zone projects get a credit too.

md_ez.label: Maryland Enterprise Zone
md_ez.desc: Zones where businesses may be eligible for real-property and income-tax credits for job creation and investment (Maryland Department of Commerce).

nj_uez.label: New Jersey Urban Enterprise Zone
nj_uez.one: a New Jersey Urban Enterprise Zone
nj_uez.desc: Designated urban areas where retailers the state certifies charge half the sales tax (3.3125%) on goods sold in person, not on meals, alcohol, cigarettes, vehicles or services, and businesses can get other state incentives; the 32 zones run through June 30, 2032 (New Jersey Department of Community Affairs).

or_ez.label: Oregon Enterprise Zone
or_ez.desc: Zones sponsored by cities, counties, ports and tribes where new business investment is exempt from local property tax for three to five years, longer in some rural zones (Business Oregon).

tn_tdz.label: Tennessee Tourism Development Zone
tn_tdz.desc: Zones around a convention center or other public use facility where the growth in state and local sales tax collected inside the zone is set aside to pay for the facility (Convention Center and Tourism Development Financing Act), administered by the Department of Revenue.

va_tz.label: Virginia technology zone
va_tz.desc: Zones a county or city sets up under state law (Code 58.1-3850), where new and expanding technology businesses can get reduced local taxes and fees, such as the business license (BPOL) tax, for a set period.

va_acd.label: Virginia arts and cultural district
va_acd.desc: Districts a county or city designates under state law (Code 15.2-1129.1), where it may offer tax and fee incentives to arts and cultural businesses and venues.

rva_care.label: Richmond CARE area
rva_care.desc: Commercial corridors in the City of Richmond's Commercial Area Revitalization Effort, where businesses and commercial property owners can get rebates for security, exterior and interior rehabilitation (not new construction).

va_ez.label: Virginia Enterprise Zone
va_ez.desc: Zones where businesses can get state grants for new jobs and for investing in real property (Virginia Department of Housing and Community Development), often with local incentives too.

tx_ez.label: Texas Enterprise Zone block groups
tx_ez.desc: Census block groups where at least 20% of residents live in poverty, on the state's current list (2020 block groups). A project there that its city or county nominates can get a state sales and use tax refund (Texas Enterprise Zone Program). Distressed counties, federal zones and defense base areas also qualify but are not drawn here.

pa_koz.label: Pennsylvania Keystone Opportunity Zone site
pa_koz.desc: Designated parcels where a business can be exempt from most state and local taxes, including corporate income, sales and use, and property taxes, until the designation expires (Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development).

la_ez.label: Louisiana Enterprise Zone block groups
la_ez.desc: Census block groups that qualify for the Louisiana Enterprise Zone program (Louisiana Economic Development), where a business that adds jobs could get a credit for each new job and a state sales-tax rebate or investment credit. The program took no new projects after June 30, 2025 (Louisiana Economic Development); projects already enrolled keep their benefits.

nc_ura.label: North Carolina redevelopment area
nc_ura.desc: Areas a city designates under the Urban Redevelopment Law, where its redevelopment plan lets it buy and assemble property, clear blight and offer sites for new housing and businesses (G.S. 160A-500 and after).

ga_ez.label: Georgia Enterprise Zone
ga_ez.desc: Areas a city or county designates under the Enterprise Zone Employment Act, where businesses that invest and create jobs can get local property tax exemptions and reduced local fees for a set number of years (O.C.G.A. 36-88; Department of Community Affairs).

ga_soz.label: Georgia State Opportunity Zone
ga_soz.desc: Areas designated by the Georgia Department of Community Affairs (not federal Opportunity Zones) where a business that creates at least two jobs can claim the state's highest job tax credit.

il_rez.label: Illinois River Edge Redevelopment Zone
il_rez.one: an Illinois River Edge Redevelopment Zone
il_rez.desc: Zones along rivers in a few Illinois cities where cleanup and redevelopment of environmentally challenged sites earn state tax credits, much like an enterprise zone (River Edge Redevelopment Zone Act).

oh_ez.label: Ohio Enterprise Zone
oh_ez.desc: Areas where a city or county can exempt part of the property tax on a business's new or improved real property when it invests and adds jobs, by agreement for a set number of years (Ohio Enterprise Zone program, Ohio Revised Code 5709.61 to 5709.69).

oh_cra.label: Ohio Community Reinvestment Area
oh_cra.desc: Areas where a city, village or county exempts part or all of the property-tax increase from building or renovating homes or commercial buildings, for a set number of years (Community Reinvestment Area program, Ohio Revised Code 3735.65 to 3735.70).

ok_ez.label: Oklahoma Enterprise Zone
ok_ez.desc: Census tracts that qualify as enterprise zones for fiscal 2027 (Oklahoma Department of Commerce), plus grandfathered zones: businesses there can get doubled investment and jobs tax credits and sales-tax relief.

hi_ez.label: Hawaii Enterprise Zone
hi_ez.desc: Zones where eligible businesses can get state general excise and income tax relief for up to seven years; for businesses joining from July 1, 2026, up to nine years, or twelve for manufacturing and agriculture (Act 182 of 2026; Hawaii Department of Business, Economic Development and Tourism).

ny_boa.label: New York Brownfield Opportunity Area
ny_boa.one: a New York Brownfield Opportunity Area
ny_boa.desc: Areas with community revitalization plans designated by the New York Department of State, where brownfield cleanup projects can earn a bonus on the state brownfield tax credit.

ny_enzone.label: New York Environmental Zone (En-Zone)
ny_enzone.desc: Census tracts with high poverty and unemployment where brownfield redevelopment earns a larger state tax credit (Brownfield Cleanup Program).

de_ddd.label: Delaware Downtown Development District
de_ddd.desc: Downtown districts designated by the state where private investment can get a state rebate of part of its cost, plus local incentives (Delaware State Housing Authority).

ca_eifd.label: California Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District (EIFD)
ca_eifd.desc: California's tax increment districts since the 2012 end of redevelopment agencies: the growth in property-tax revenue from new development pays for public infrastructure, with no new tax.

bid.label: Business improvement district
bid.desc: Commercial districts that pay an added assessment (usually on property; on hotel stays in a tourism district) for services such as cleaning, security, marketing and events, run by a district management organization.

chi_ssa.label: Chicago Special Service Area
chi_ssa.desc: Commercial districts that pay a small added property tax for services such as cleaning, security, marketing and small-business support, run by a local service provider.

ca_dac.label: California SB 535 disadvantaged community
ca_dac.desc: Census tracts the California EPA designates as disadvantaged (CalEnviroScreen): they get minimum shares of California Climate Investments funding and priority in many state grant and incentive programs (Health and Safety Code 39711-39713).

ca_lic.label: California AB 1550 low-income community
ca_lic.desc: Census tracts with household incomes at or below 80% of the statewide median or the state income limits for low-income households: California Climate Investments must put a share of their funding into projects in or benefiting these communities (Health and Safety Code 39713, AB 1550 of 2016).

ca_dct.label: California designated census tract
ca_dct.desc: Census tracts in the top quarter of California for both unemployment and poverty, designated by the Department of Finance every five years (Government Code 13073.5; January 2024 designation from the 2017-2021 ACS): state contract bidders that hire or work in them can get a preference under the Target Area Contract Preference Act, and they set the area for the New Employment Credit.

co_rjs.label: Colorado Rural Jump-Start county
co_rjs.desc: Distressed rural counties taking part in Rural Jump-Start: new businesses and their new hires can get state income tax credits and sales and use tax exemptions (C.R.S. 39-30.5).

co_coal.label: Colorado coal transition community
co_coal.desc: Counties and towns the Office of Just Transition names as coal transition communities (Tier 1 or 2): priority for Just Transition grants and enhanced enterprise zone and Rural Jump-Start incentives.

dc_dez.label: DC Development Enterprise Zone
dc_dez.desc: Census tracts with 10% or more poverty where businesses get Certified Business Enterprise preference points in District contracting (Department of Small and Local Business Development).

dc_npta.label: DC nonprofit tax abatement zone
dc_npta.desc: Neighborhoods where a nonprofit that buys and occupies a building can get a real property tax abatement (D.C. Code 47-857.11 and after).

dc_super.label: DC supermarket tax incentive area
dc_super.desc: Areas where a qualified supermarket can get a real property tax exemption, a sales tax exemption on building materials and a business license fee exemption (D.C. Code 47-3801 and after).

fl_rao.label: Florida Rural Area of Opportunity
fl_rao.desc: Rural counties and cities designated by the Governor: waivers of match and eligibility rules and priority for state economic development incentives and rural grants (s. 288.0656, F.S.).

ga_ldct.label: Georgia less developed census tract
ga_ldct.desc: Tracts designated each year in the Department of Community Affairs' census tract rankings (2026 list), where a business that creates jobs can claim the job tax credit at the Tier 1 rate ($3,500 a job) (O.C.G.A. 48-7-40.1(b)).

ga_mz.label: Georgia military zone
ga_mz.desc: Tracts near military installations designated as military zones (2026 list, each with its own effective date), where a business that creates jobs can claim the job tax credit at the Tier 1 rate ($3,500 a job) (Department of Community Affairs; O.C.G.A. 48-7-40.1(c)).

ga_rz.label: Georgia Rural Zone
ga_rz.desc: Rural downtowns designated for five years where businesses can claim job, investment (25% of a purchase) and rehabilitation tax credits (O.C.G.A. 48-7-40.30).

ks_roz.label: Kansas Rural Opportunity Zone
ks_roz.desc: Counties where new residents could get up to five years of Kansas income tax waived and student loan repayment of up to $15,000; residents had to arrive before 2026 and the tax credit ends with tax year 2026.

md_ezfa.label: Maryland Enterprise Zone focus area
md_ezfa.desc: Parts of enterprise zones in Baltimore City and Prince George's County where the income tax and real property tax credits are larger (Maryland Department of Commerce).

md_rise.label: Maryland RISE Zone
md_rise.desc: Regional Institution Strategic Enterprise zones around universities and other anchors: real property tax credits and income tax credits for businesses that locate or expand there (Maryland Department of Commerce).

ne_ez.label: Nebraska Enterprise Zone
ne_ez.desc: Zones designated by the Department of Economic Development where projects get preference in its job training, innovation, housing and site development programs (Enterprise Zone Act, Neb. Rev. Stat. 13-2101 and after).

ne_ihub.label: Nebraska Innovation Hub eligible tract
ne_ihub.desc: Tracts with poverty over 19.9% and unemployment over 5%, eligible for the Department of Economic Development's Innovation Hub grants.

nh_erz.label: New Hampshire Economic Revitalization Zone
nh_erz.desc: Zones where projects that create jobs can get business profits and business enterprise tax credits (RSA 162-N); the program runs until January 1, 2028, and each zone is reviewed every five years (Department of Business and Economic Affairs).

nh_79e.label: New Hampshire 79-E district
nh_79e.desc: Districts a town has adopted under RSA 79-E, where a building's property tax assessment can be held at its pre-rehabilitation value for a period after a substantial rehabilitation.

nj_qit.label: New Jersey Qualified Incentive Tract
nj_qit.desc: Tracts where projects get larger Emerge job tax credits and larger Aspire redevelopment tax credits (New Jersey Economic Development Authority; Economic Recovery Act of 2020).

nj_innov.label: New Jersey Innovation Zone
nj_innov.desc: Newark, New Brunswick and Camden, where investors get bonus Angel Investor tax credits and innovation programs give priority (New Jersey Economic Development Authority).

nj_anr.label: New Jersey area in need of redevelopment
nj_anr.one: an area in need of redevelopment
nj_anr.desc: Areas a municipality has declared in need of redevelopment under the Local Redevelopment and Housing Law (N.J.S.A. 40A:12A), where it can adopt a redevelopment plan, grant long-term tax exemptions (payments in lieu of taxes) and, if the declaration allows, use eminent domain. The Department of Community Affairs' map is incomplete for declarations before July 2003.

nj_nrtc.label: New Jersey Neighborhood Revitalization Tax Credit neighborhood
nj_nrtc.one: a Neighborhood Revitalization Tax Credit neighborhood
nj_nrtc.desc: Neighborhoods with a state-approved revitalization plan, where businesses that fund the plan's projects get a credit of 100% of the contribution against state business taxes (Department of Community Affairs).

nj_ms.label: Main Street New Jersey district
nj_ms.one: a Main Street New Jersey district
nj_ms.desc: Downtowns in the state's Main Street program, which gives their management organizations training, technical help and grants (Department of Community Affairs).

nj_fdc.label: New Jersey Food Desert Community
nj_fdc.desc: Communities designated under the Food Desert Relief Act, where supermarkets and food access projects can get tax credits, grants and loans (New Jersey Economic Development Authority).

ok_qj5.label: Oklahoma Quality Jobs 5% county
ok_qj5.desc: Counties where Quality Jobs projects can get the higher 5% payroll rebate (Oklahoma Department of Commerce, 2026 list).

ok_seqj.label: Oklahoma Small Employer Quality Jobs county
ok_seqj.one: a Small Employer Quality Jobs county
ok_seqj.desc: High-unemployment, high-poverty counties with lower job and wage thresholds for Small Employer Quality Jobs (Oklahoma Department of Commerce, 2026 list).

va_tob.label: Virginia Tobacco Region locality
va_tob.desc: The 40 counties and cities where projects can get Tobacco Region Revitalization Commission grants, including its performance-based Tobacco Region Opportunity Fund.

hi_hcda.label: Hawaii Community Development Authority district
hi_hcda.one: a Hawaii Community Development Authority district
hi_hcda.desc: State community development districts where the Hawaii Community Development Authority, not the county, plans and zones land and guides redevelopment (HRS chapter 206E); He‘eia's district is for agriculture and Native Hawaiian culture.

hnl_tod.label: Honolulu TOD special district
hnl_tod.desc: Rail station areas where the City and County of Honolulu has adopted transit-oriented development special district rules by ordinance, which set the zoning and design standards for new building (Department of Planning and Permitting).

id_ura.label: Idaho urban renewal area
id_ura.desc: Urban renewal revenue allocation areas, where the growth in property tax pays for improvements (Idaho Code 50-2901 and after); mapped by the Idaho State Tax Commission statewide.

nh_tif.label: New Hampshire TIF district
nh_tif.desc: Tax increment financing districts adopted by New Hampshire towns and cities under RSA 162-K; mapped statewide by the Office of Planning and Development.

dc_gs.label: DC Great Streets corridor
dc_gs.desc: Commercial corridors where retailers and service businesses can apply for Great Streets small business capital grants (Deputy Mayor for Planning and Economic Development).

dc_npf.label: DC Neighborhood Prosperity Fund tract
dc_npf.desc: Distressed tracts where commercial and mixed-use projects can apply for Neighborhood Prosperity Fund gap financing (Deputy Mayor for Planning and Economic Development).

la_cd.label: Louisiana Cultural District
la_cd.desc: Districts where original art sells free of sales tax and buildings can qualify for state historic rehabilitation tax credits (La. R.S. 47:305.57 and 47:6019).

la_edd.label: Louisiana economic development district
la_edd.desc: Districts created by a parish or city under state law (La. R.S. 33:9038.31 and after, and special acts) that can levy their own sales or hotel occupancy tax, or pledge tax increments, to pay for development inside the district; where the state's rate listing includes a district's sales tax, it is noted with the rates.

la_ms.label: Louisiana Main Street district
la_ms.desc: Designated Main Street downtowns that get state technical help and can apply for Main Street restoration grants (Louisiana Office of Cultural Development).

md_ae.label: Maryland Arts and Entertainment District
md_ae.desc: Districts with a property tax credit for renovating artists' space, an income tax subtraction for artists' work made there and an admissions and amusement tax exemption (Maryland State Arts Council).

md_ms.label: Main Street Maryland community
md_ms.desc: Downtowns in the state's Main Street program (Designated, Connected or Aspiring), with technical help and priority for revitalization funding (Department of Housing and Community Development).

md_sc.label: Maryland Sustainable Community
md_sc.desc: Areas whose designation opens the state's revitalization programs (Community Legacy, Strategic Demolition, Neighborhood BusinessWorks and others) and gives priority for state historic tax credits (Department of Housing and Community Development).

md_brni.label: Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative area
md_brni.desc: Neighborhoods in Baltimore City and nearby counties where community groups can apply for state grants for housing and business investment (Department of Housing and Community Development).

ma_tdi.label: MassDevelopment Transformative Development Initiative district
ma_tdi.desc: Gateway City downtown districts that get MassDevelopment fellows, technical help, equity investments and place-based grants while the cohort is active.

ny_dri.label: New York Downtown Revitalization Initiative area
ny_dri.desc: Downtowns awarded $10 million or more in state grants for projects inside the boundary (Department of State).

ny_nyf.label: NY Forward area
ny_nyf.desc: Smaller downtowns awarded about $4.5 million in state grants for projects inside the boundary (Department of State).

ok_ms.label: Oklahoma Main Street district
ok_ms.desc: Active Main Street program districts, with state technical help, design and training services (Oklahoma Main Street Center).

ct_distressed.label: Connecticut distressed municipality
ct_distressed.desc: Towns the Department of Economic and Community Development lists each year as distressed by unemployment, income, poverty and housing measures: priority for some state grants, and property tax exemptions for manufacturing and other qualifying projects (CGS 32-9p). Towns that drop off keep the status for a grace period.

vt_desig.label: Vermont designated downtown or village center
vt_desig.desc: Designated downtowns, village centers, new town centers, growth centers and neighborhood development areas: tax credits for historic, code and facade work, priority for state grants, and permit relief for housing (24 V.S.A. ch. 76A). Act 181 of 2024 is replacing these designations; their benefits continue during the change.

fl_bfa.label: Florida designated brownfield area
fl_bfa.desc: Areas designated by local resolution where cleanup can earn voluntary cleanup tax credits, and projects a $2,500-a-job bonus refund, a sales tax refund on building materials and loan guarantees (s. 376.80, F.S.).

nj_bda.label: New Jersey Brownfield Development Area
nj_bda.desc: Areas where the Department of Environmental Protection manages cleanup planning with the community and gives priority for Hazardous Discharge Site Remediation Fund grants.

nc_bf.label: North Carolina brownfields site
nc_bf.desc: Properties in the state's Brownfields Program; under a brownfields agreement, improvements get a five-year partial property tax exclusion (G.S. 105-277.13) and the developer gets liability protection.

chi_tsl.label: Chicago Transit Served Location
chi_tsl.desc: Land within a half mile of a CTA or Metra rail station or a quarter mile of a listed CTA bus corridor, where the Connected Communities Ordinance removes parking minimums and allows more homes (Department of Planning and Development).

nyc_tz.label: New York City Transit Zone
nyc_tz.desc: Areas where City of Yes for Housing Opportunity removes or reduces required residential parking: the Manhattan Core and Long Island City, the Inner Transit Zone (none required) and the Outer Transit Zone (reduced) (Department of City Planning).

la_toc.label: Los Angeles Transit Oriented Communities tier
la_toc.desc: Land within a half mile of a major transit stop, in tiers 1 to 4, where housing with affordable units gets density, floor area and parking incentives (Measure JJJ; Department of City Planning). City Planning's housing policy summary says the program is set to expire in 2026, and the Citywide Housing Incentive Program, in use since February 2025, carries its transit incentives forward (its Mixed Income Incentive Program and transit-oriented incentive areas); confirm a site's status with City Planning.

ca_hqta.label: California high-quality transit area
ca_hqta.desc: Land within a half mile of a major transit stop or along a high-quality bus corridor, where CEQA review is streamlined for many housing and mixed-use projects (Public Resources Code 21155, 21099). Only within a half mile of a major transit stop are cities barred from requiring parking for most projects (AB 2097, Gov. Code 65863.2); the corridor parts of these areas are not covered by that rule (Caltrans statewide map).

ma_mbta.label: MBTA Communities multifamily district
ma_mbta.desc: Districts zoned for multifamily housing by right at 15 or more homes an acre, most near transit stations, in towns found compliant with the MBTA Communities law (M.G.L. c. 40A s. 3A; MassGIS).

md_tod.label: Maryland designated TOD site
md_tod.desc: Station areas the state designates for transit-oriented development: priority for state funding and incentives and eligibility for tax increment financing (Maryland Department of Transportation).

pa_criz.label: Pennsylvania City Revitalization and Improvement Zone
pa_criz.one: a City Revitalization and Improvement Zone
pa_criz.desc: Zones in Bethlehem, Lancaster, Tamaqua, Erie and Reading where the growth in state and local taxes paid by businesses in the zone (above each business's baseline, plus the taxes of new businesses), sales tax included, goes to repay bonds for development projects there instead of to the general fund (Pennsylvania Department of Revenue).

phl_toc.label: Philadelphia transit-oriented overlay
phl_toc.desc: Zoning overlays around Market-Frankford Line stations with density and height bonuses and reduced parking (Philadelphia Zoning Code 14-513).

mia_rtz.label: Miami-Dade Rapid Transit Zone
mia_rtz.desc: Land around Metrorail, Metromover and busway stations under county zoning, with its own development standards and incentives (Miami-Dade County Code ch. 33C).

metc_tod.label: Twin Cities TOD grant area
metc_tod.desc: Areas eligible for the Metropolitan Council's Livable Communities transit-oriented development grants: light rail, commuter rail and bus rapid transit station areas and high-frequency bus corridors.

dal_tod.label: Dallas transit-oriented parking area
dal_tod.desc: Half-mile areas around DART light rail, commuter rail and streetcar stations where the 2025 parking code amendment removes or reduces required parking (City of Dallas).

aus_etod.label: Austin Equitable TOD overlay
aus_etod.desc: Overlay around planned light rail and MetroRapid stations where projects with affordable housing can build higher, up to 90 or 120 feet (Ordinance 20240516-005).

dc_tpa.label: DC transit parking reduction area
dc_tpa.desc: Land within a half mile of a Metrorail station or a quarter mile of a priority bus corridor, where the zoning regulations reduce required parking (11-C DCMR 702).

bay_pda.label: Bay Area Priority Development Area
bay_pda.desc: Locally nominated growth areas near transit, adopted by ABAG and MTC, that get priority for regional planning and transportation grants (Plan Bay Area 2050+).

cid.label: Community improvement district (CID)
cid.desc: Districts whose owners or voters approve an added tax inside the boundary for improvements and services: in Missouri and Kansas usually an added sales tax (in Missouri also property taxes or special assessments), often for one shopping center or block; in Georgia an added property tax on commercial and industrial property for transportation, safety and upkeep (RSMo 67.1401 to 67.1571; K.S.A. 12-6a26 and after; Georgia Constitution art. IX, sec. VII).

tdd.label: Transportation development district (TDD)
tdd.desc: Missouri districts that add a sales tax of up to 1% (or a property tax or special assessment) inside the boundary to pay for roads, parking and other transportation projects, often for one shopping center (RSMo 238.200 to 238.275).

il_ssa.label: Illinois special service area (outside Chicago)
il_ssa.desc: Areas where an Illinois city, village or county levies an added property tax or fee to pay for services or improvements that benefit only that area, such as downtown upkeep and promotion or streets and stormwater (Special Service Area Tax Law, 35 ILCS 200/27-5 and after).

il_bdd.label: Illinois business development district
il_bdd.desc: Districts where an Illinois city or village can add up to 1% to the sales tax and up to 1% to the hotel tax and spend the revenue on the district's redevelopment plan, for up to 23 years (Business District Development and Redevelopment Law, 65 ILCS 5/11-74.3).

ia_ms.label: Main Street Iowa district
ia_ms.desc: Downtown and neighborhood commercial districts accredited in Main Street Iowa (Iowa Economic Development Authority), which get its training, design and technical help and can apply for Main Street Iowa Challenge Grants.

visitor.rule: an area (its tracts summed) has a visitor economy when at least 50 of its homes are seasonal and they are at least 3 times the national share of housing units, or it has at least 5 lodging places and lodging places per 1,000 residents are at or above the 95th percentile of places with 1,000+ residents

public_property.rule: Parcels that large cities publish, in their official GIS layers, as owned by a land bank or land reutilization authority (land bank), owned by the city, county or another public agency, surplus land included (city or public owned), or vacant (citywide vacant-lot or vacant-building layers, any owner). Where a layer's owner field mixes public agencies and private owners, only parcels owned by a public agency or a land bank are counted, decided by a list of public-agency names; no owner names are kept. A parcel listed twice (centroids within 5 m and shapes overlapping by half, or points within 1 m) counts once, in the 2024 census tract that holds a point inside its shape (or the nearest tract within 1 km, for waterfront lots outside the shoreline-clipped tract shapes). Acres are the mapped parcel area, or the stated acreage for layers of points; vacant building footprints carry none. Only the listed cities are covered, each as its layer stands (vintages differ), so a tract outside them, or with none, is not evidence of no public or vacant land.
